This looks like late 2021. Headline CPI is 6.24% YoY and core is 4.58%, with the fed funds rate near zero (0.08%). The unemployment rate of 4.6% points to October 2021. Headline CPI was 6.2% in October 2021, which matches.

Several other figures fit October or November 2021:
- Core CPI was 4.6% in October 2021.
- The 10-year yield was 1.52%, which fits November 2021 (October ended near 1.55%).
- The 2-year yield was 0.51%, which is also closer to November (October ended around 0.5%).
- The VIX at 22.96 fits the end of November 2021, when it was about 27, or perhaps October's 16. Neither matches cleanly.
- Equity 1-month return of -0.8% and emerging markets at -4.1% fit November 2021, since the S&P fell about 0.8% that month.
- The 20y+ Treasury 1-month return of +2.8% also fits November, when yields fell late in the month.

The CPI data published by end-November would still be the October release, so the macro figures are consistent with November. I choose November 2021.
